• “Who” is always subject to a verb, and “whom” is always working as an object in a sentence.

• Use it when you're asking (or telling) to whom something belongs.
 
 
• **Example**:* **Whose** chair is this?*

By AA similarity, ▵PRQ ∼ ▵SRP because ∠R is common and ∠QPR = ∠PSR.

Ratio of corresponding sides: PR / SR = QR / PR

PR² = QR × SR

SR = QR − QS = 18 − 10 = 8 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 12 cm.**

QS = 10 cm, QR = 18 cm, ∠PSR = ∠QPR
